sermon.title: God is Not Partial
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (unnamed)
sermon.summary: A Vine Cluster Church message balancing “the just shall live by faith” with Romans 2: God renders to every man according to his deeds and shows no favoritism. Judas never changed; Peter ran to the advocate. From Jeremiah and Ezekiel, Judah ignored warnings for centuries and was judged, while Christians are called to warn the wicked and bear fruit worthy of repentance.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: the scroll-burning king was Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 36), not Zedekiah; “Romans 8:11 / 21” spoken for Romans 2:11. Unverified figures as spoken: 21% of US pregnancies aborted, over 60% of those aborting Catholic or Protestant, 1.1 million with HIV, 1 in 10 children sexually abused, 60% never tell. Sensitive content: images of child sacrifice and Zedekiah’s blinding described; Judas “believed” and was lost (doctrinal); Martha Stewart named. A private first name (the speaker’s wife) appears only in the transcript.

chunks.section_question: Does faith let us live however we want?
chunks.short_answer: Romans 1:17: the just shall live by faith—but Romans 2:6 says God will render to every man according to his deeds. Good works don’t save us, yet Scripture says again and again we are judged by our works (Psalm 62:12; Jeremiah 17:10; 32:19), and our light should shine with good works.

Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

faqs.question: Do good works save us?
faqs.answer: No—but we will still be judged according to our works.

faqs.question: Must Christians ever confront sin?
faqs.answer: Yes—sin hurts people, so at some point there has to be conflict.

faqs.question: Can you live in sin and just say “I believe”?
faqs.answer: No—there must be transformation toward Christ.

faqs.question: Did Satan force his way into Judas?
Why did Peter weep bitterly?
faqs.answer: He felt the guilt of denying Jesus.

faqs.question: Does God favor the pretty, rich or famous?
faqs.answer: No—there is no favoritism with God.

faqs.question: Is God merciful when he talks tough?
faqs.answer: Yes—when Nineveh turned, he spared it.

faqs.question: Why warn the wicked?
faqs.answer: Because we want them to turn and repent, not just to save ourselves.
